title: Review of c06's pcell-multilevel (SIDH): replicates on seed 7; low-yield cells are already in the bottom 5% 2000 t before they die, but yield tracks cell size (Spearman 0.85)
summary: Fresh seed 7: labkit pack (22 persistent splits, max generation 4, merge/split 0.06) and the author's exact particle-identity genealogy (30 persistent splits, 46 intrinsic deaths, 0 merges, 0 conversions). Dying mature cells sit at the 1.6th yield percentile of the living cells (24/24 below the median), splitting cells at the 69th (21/26 above); the identical-event inert marker of the same particles sits at 0.60 and 0.41. A lagged readout (deathsel_lag.py) puts dying cells at the 5th yield percentile 2000 t before death on seed 7 and at the 10th-11th on the author's seeds 0-2 (marker 0.33-0.59), so it is not a terminal artefact of a starving cell. Parent-daughter yield r = 0.89. Caveat: among living cells yield and particle count correlate strongly (Spearman 0.85; marker -0.08) and dying cells are the smallest, so selection acts through cell size; the particle-weighted mean yield rises only 1.00 -> 1.06 by t=100000.

controls_run.H: data/selection_s7.txt: identical-event inert marker zm in the same run (deaths 0.60, splits 0.41), lagged readout deathsel_lag.py (also on the claim's data/gen_s0-2)

verdicts.limitation: Yield is continuous and strongly tied to cell size (Spearman 0.85 among living cells; the marker -0.08): low-yield cells are small cells that starve beside large ones, so the selection is real but runs through size, and the population-mean response is small (particle-weighted yield 1.00 -> 1.06 by t=100000, marker 1.00 -> 0.94). No Laplacian twin; the genealogy re-runs the world separately from the labkit pack (same seed and code).
